**Answer: the chain is Blazor `Checkout` page → `BasketState` → HTTP POST to Ordering.API → MediatR `IdentifiedCommandHandler` → `CreateOrderCommandHandler` → `OrderingContext.SaveEntitiesAsync`, where `base.SaveChangesAsync` writes the order row.**

Handlers in order (WebApp = the storefront, Ordering.API = the service that persists):

1. **`Checkout.HandleSubmitAsync`** — the checkout `EditForm` posts to it: `<EditForm ... FormName="checkout" OnSubmit="@HandleSubmitAsync" Enhance>` (`src/WebApp/Components/Pages/Checkout/Checkout.razor:12`); after validation it calls `HandleValidSubmitAsync` (`src/WebApp/Components/Pages/Checkout/Checkout.razor:105-108`).
2. **`Checkout.HandleValidSubmitAsync`** — sets `Info.CardTypeId = 1`, calls `Basket.CheckoutAsync(Info)`, then navigates to `user/orders` (`src/WebApp/Components/Pages/Checkout/Checkout.razor:111-116`).
3. **`BasketState.CheckoutAsync`** — assigns a `RequestId`, resolves buyer id/user name, fetches basket items (`src/WebApp/Services/BasketState.cs:78-89`), then calls `OrderingService.CreateOrder` (`src/WebApp/Services/BasketState.cs:107`) and clears the basket (`src/WebApp/Services/BasketState.cs:108`).
4. **`OrderingService.CreateOrder`** — HTTP `POST /api/Orders/` with an `x-requestid` header (`src/WebApp/Services/OrderingService.cs:12-15`).
5. **`OrdersApi.CreateOrderAsync`** (Ordering.API) — routed by `api.MapPost("/", CreateOrderAsync)` (`src/Ordering.API/Apis/OrdersApi.cs:17`); it masks the card number, builds a `CreateOrderCommand`, wraps it in `IdentifiedCommand<CreateOrderCommand, bool>` and does `services.Mediator.Send(requestCreateOrder)` (`src/Ordering.API/Apis/OrdersApi.cs:118-156`).
6. **MediatR pipeline behaviors** run around that send: `LoggingBehavior`, `ValidatorBehavior`, `TransactionBehavior` — the last one opens the DB transaction/execution strategy (`src/Ordering.API/Application/Behaviors/TransactionBehavior.cs:20-32`).
7. **`CreateOrderIdentifiedCommandHandler`** (derives from `IdentifiedCommandHandler<CreateOrderCommand, bool>`, declared at `src/Ordering.API/Application/Commands/CreateOrderCommandHandler.cs:56-58`) — its inherited **`IdentifiedCommandHandler.Handle`** does the idempotency check via `IRequestManager.ExistAsync` / `CreateRequestForCommandAsync` and then forwards the inner `CreateOrderCommand` through the mediator (`src/Ordering.API/Application/Commands/IdentifiedCommandHandler.cs:39-51`; the method continues to line 105 — I read its first half, the class summary states it "just enqueues the original inner command", `src/Ordering.API/Application/Commands/IdentifiedCommandHandler.cs:3-6`).
8. **`CreateOrderCommandHandler.Handle`** — publishes `OrderStartedIntegrationEvent`, builds the `Order` aggregate plus items (`src/Ordering.API/Application/Commands/CreateOrderCommandHandler.cs:29-45`), then `_orderRepository.Add(order)` (`src/Ordering.API/Application/Commands/CreateOrderCommandHandler.cs:49`) and `return await _orderRepository.UnitOfWork.SaveEntitiesAsync(cancellationToken)` (`src/Ordering.API/Application/Commands/CreateOrderCommandHandler.cs:51`).
9. **`OrderRepository.Add`** — `_context.Orders.Add(order).Entity`, i.e. only EF change-tracking, not yet a DB write (`src/Ordering.Infrastructure/Repositories/OrderRepository.cs:15-17`); `UnitOfWork` is the `OrderingContext` (`src/Ordering.Infrastructure/Repositories/OrderRepository.cs:8`).
10. **`OrderingContext.SaveEntitiesAsync`** — first `await _mediator.DispatchDomainEventsAsync(this)` (`src/Ordering.Infrastructure/OrderingContext.cs`, in the method starting ~line 47; dispatch helper at `src/Ordering.Infrastructure/MediatorExtension.cs:5-19`), which runs the domain-event handler **`ValidateOrAddBuyerAggregateWhenOrderStartedDomainEventHandler.Handle`** (`src/Ordering.API/Application/DomainEventHandlers/ValidateOrAddBuyerAggregateWhenOrderStartedDomainEventHandler.cs:20-47`) in the same transaction.

**The line that writes the order to the database** is `_ = await base.SaveChangesAsync(cancellationToken);` inside `OrderingContext.SaveEntitiesAsync` (`src/Ordering.Infrastructure/OrderingContext.cs`, roughly line 59 — I counted it from the file contents rather than reading a line-numbered gutter, so the number may be off by a line or two; the method is uniquely identifiable by its "After executing this line all the changes ... will be committed" comment). The surrounding transaction is committed by `TransactionBehavior` (`src/Ordering.API/Application/Behaviors/TransactionBehavior.cs:20-32`).

Note: an earlier DB write also happens on the same request path before the order itself — `RequestManager.CreateRequestForCommandAsync` saves the idempotency `ClientRequest` row (`src/Ordering.API/Application/Commands/IdentifiedCommandHandler.cs:48`), and `OrderingIntegrationEventService.AddAndSaveEventAsync` persists the integration-event log (`src/Ordering.API/Application/Commands/CreateOrderCommandHandler.cs:33`). Those write different tables, not the order.
